Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-discovery)

Hi Jenna 

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from todays discovery and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve kept this brief.

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Strict data residency & PHI handling for clinical logs (must stay within US region).
- Latency sensitivity for live clinician assistant (99th perc target ~150ms).
- Current infra: self-hosted GPU cluster (on-prem K8s) with licensed model weights.
- Desire to reduce operational burden and get predictable per-token costs.

Deployment options we discussed (short):
- Hosted API (fastest to go live)  good for POC but may not meet residency/compliance now.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools)  predictable throughput, isolation, good fit if you can move traffic to a committed pool in a cloud region.
- Private (VPC / on-prem)  supports air-gapped or on-prem licensing scenarios and full control over keys/audit logs.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you share a short infra summary (node specs, k8s version, networking restrictions)  I attached a one-page infra template to make this quick.
2) Would you be open to a technical deep-dive with Ethan (our SE) to map the migration path for model weights and runtime? Suggest Wed or Thu next week.
3) I’ll have Rafael put together a high-level cost/TOC compare (Dedicated vs Private) once we get the infra answers.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf (short matrix: Hosted / Dedicated / Private tradeoffs)

Thanks  we’ll keep this lightweight.


Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-discovery)

Thanks Marissa  appreciate the clear recap.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Data residency: US-only is non-negotiable for initial launch (we can revisit EU later).
- PHI: we need SOC2 + HIPAA alignment and an understanding of key management (customer-managed keys preferred).
- Current infra: on-prem Kubernetes (v1.24) with 8xA100-equivalent GPUs across two racks; model weights are licensed from a third party and cannot leave on-prem in current contract terms without amendment.
- Timeline: target pilot in Q4 (Nov) with production H1 2027 — but procurement needs cost signals this quarter.

We’re definitely interested in Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) given the model licensing constraint, but would like to see the Dedicated cost comparison in parallel to evaluate tradeoffs if the vendor contract can be amended.

I’ll coordinate with procurement for the infra matrix  attaching a brief that outlines our network policy and a permissions contact (network@novahealth.ai).

Forwarding the infra contact below for scheduling.

Best,
Jenna

Marissa / Jenna 

Thanks for the details, Jenna  that helps a lot. A few notes from infra/solutions perspective:

- Given the contractual restriction that licensed weights cannot leave on-prem, Private (on-prem) is the cleanest path operationally. We can ship a Private control plane and on-prem runtime that keeps weights resident while we manage inference endpoints.
- Dedicated (cloud-based) is still possible if the vendor contract is amended to allow cloud hosting; it typically reduces ops burden but adds a contractual step.
- For cost comparisons I’ll produce: 1) Dedicated reserved monthly estimate, 2) Private on-prem integration estimate (one-time integration + monthly support/maintenance).

What we need from Nova to size accurately:
- Exact GPU model / memory per node and total GPU count (you listed 8x A100-equivalent  can you confirm model & memory?)
- Network egress policies and whether outbound connections to a Redwood control plane are permitted (we have an air-gapped option if not).
- Any specific KMS/HSM provider details if you need customer-managed keys.

I’ll slot a 60-min technical deep-dive with Ethan and our infra lead. Proposed times: Wed 07/29 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 07/30 13:00-14:00 PT. Marissa  can you coordinate?
